name: Nora Santos

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I am from the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to employers, AI companies, unions, parties or government. Your answers are confidential. What happens on an ordinary day at your accounting firm?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I open the bakery accounts first because the owner sends the bread sales before the invoices, and I match the two before anyone files a return. I lead the tax team and enjoy explaining a difficult number without making a client feel foolish; chasing missing papers at closing time is the part I dread. I am 43, with a master's degree and a chartered accountancy qualification. I use AI now and then for a first outline of a client letter, then check every figure and write the final answer myself. My partner Paolo works delivery shifts, and we have two school-age children and a mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If AI stays small, my bakery files still need a person to check the figures. A draft letter might save a few minutes, but the tax deadlines and household bills remain.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell my team to use the same review checklist before a return leaves the office. I would tell clients they still have a person to call about a mistake.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I am good at this work but paid below other senior accountants, and we have less than a month's expenses set aside. My partner Paolo's delivery hours change each week; the mortgage does not, and there are few similar firms nearby.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep the paid bakery accounts and final review myself. I would put twenty from each monthly wage into a separate cash account only when our mortgage, groceries and school fares are covered, and I would continue using AI only for draft letters under the firm's current rules.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about our narrow margin even if the technology disappoints. A quiet year is helpful, but a broken washing machine would still take our spare cash.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why keep the checklist if AI barely changes?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: We have lost time before over a transposed bread-sale total. The checklist is cheaper than asking the owner to explain a wrong tax notice.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Does Paolo's work give you a cushion?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My partner Paolo can usually get some delivery shifts, but the count changes with the depot's orders. I cannot budget his best week as though it repeats every month.

say: I would keep the **review checklist** before filing returns.
I would tell clients a **named accountant** still answers errors.
think: My **low senior wage** leaves little after fixed bills.
Paolo's variable shifts cannot fill our **thin reserve** reliably.
do: Keep **paid bakery returns**, final review and approved draft-letter checks.
Deposit **twenty monthly** only after mortgage, groceries and school fares are covered.
feel: I feel **anxious** about our cash margin.
S0.quote: A quiet year is helpful, but a broken washing machine would still take our spare cash.
fieldNote: She already uses **AI occasionally** but places the human check between a draft and a tax return.
The cash deposit is conditional on **essential bills**; Paolo's variable delivery shifts do not support a larger promise.

steps.text: Keep paid bakery returns, final review and approved AI letter drafts with figure checks
Deposit twenty monthly only after mortgage groceries and school fares

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The first change would be in the letters and checking we do at our desks, not a robot in a bakery. I would expect the partners to need fewer hours from the tax team.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the partners to publish how they check AI-drafted returns and who signs them. I would tell the team to record wrong figures instead of silently fixing them after hours.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My own lead hours could be cut if the same number of clients need fewer paid reviewers. With our savings under a month and Paolo's uneven deliveries, that is a real household risk even though I know the tax rules well.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask to run a two-week paid comparison of AI drafts against last year's bakery returns, only with written partner approval and anonymised files. If the firm approves a reliable method, I would learn that approved checker on paid time; if it refuses, I would keep the authorised workflow while paid hours remain. If my hours are cut, I would seek a posted senior tax opening only with written pay, hours and a start date that cover our mortgage and school pickup.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about the wage even though I am curious about the tool. The children need their ordinary school week, not a clever demonstration.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Who watches the comparison?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My manager Inez and I would log each wrong figure and sign the result before any live use. I will not call a machine accurate because its letters sound polite.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Could you commute for a higher salary?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only if the written wage after fares still covers the mortgage and Paolo can do the confirmed pickup rota. Few local firms make that a hard condition, not a preference.

I would have staff record **wrong figures** on paid time.
think: My own **lead hours** could shrink as checking speeds up.
Few nearby firms make a **replacement wage** uncertain.
do: Run a **two-week paid comparison** on anonymised old returns only with written partner approval; otherwise keep authorised paid work.
Learn the **approved checker** on paid time only after Inez signs the result.
After cuts seek a **posted senior tax role** only if written wage after fares covers mortgage, with confirmed hours, start and pickup.
feel: I feel **anxious** about my wage and curious about the test.
S1.quote: The children need their ordinary school week, not a clever demonstration.
fieldNote: Nora's occasional draft use makes her willing to test, but **signed accuracy evidence** and paid time govern adoption.
She will not trade the mortgage and **confirmed pickup rota** for an unpriced commute to one of the few distant firms.

steps.text: Compare anonymised bakery returns for two paid weeks with written approval; otherwise keep paid checks
Learn approved checker on paid time after signed accuracy result; require written approval before live use
After cuts take posted senior job only with written after-fares mortgage-covering wage hours start and pickup

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: AGI in 2028 could make the tax judgment and client letter at once. A delivery robot in 2031 might later reach Paolo's work, but the accounting desk would face the first shock in 2028.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask our firm to state a notice and severance policy before moving client files to AGI. I would tell the team not to mistake a polished answer for a safe return.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect a large cut to my paid tax hours, perhaps the whole post, when AGI can do the thinking work cheaply. Paolo's delivery pay cannot cover the mortgage alone, and our cash would last weeks; I wake at night adding the bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I would cancel the planned new sofa and transfer its monthly instalment to emergency cash while my wages continue. I would seek posted school-district payroll posts, since I know deadlines and staff records, but I would take one only with written wage, hours and a start date that cover the mortgage and pickup; I would keep every current paid tax shift while available. In the first year after 2028, if the tax post ends, I would take only such an actual offer and use the reserve during the search.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed because I expect our main wage to fall sharply before we can save much. A plan does not pay the next mortgage bill by itself.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would school payroll be safe from AGI?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No, payroll is also desk work, and AGI could do much of it. A real paid vacancy would buy us time; I would not call it a permanent shelter.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if no post is advertised?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would not resign from work that is still paying me. If the post has already ended, I would use the small reserve while applying, and ask the lender about a temporary payment arrangement before missing a bill.

say: I would ask for **notice and severance** before AGI takes client files.
I would separate **2028 desk loss** from later delivery robots.
think: I expect a **large tax wage cut** or loss of my post.
Paolo's delivery shifts cannot cover the **mortgage** alone.
do: Cancel the **new sofa** and deposit its monthly instalment while wages continue.
Keep **paid tax shifts** while offered; after loss, use the reserve during search and contact lender before missed payments.
Take a **posted school payroll job** only with written mortgage-covering wage, hours, start and pickup fit.
feel: I feel **alarmed** by likely loss of our main wage.
S2.quote: A plan does not pay the next mortgage bill by itself.
fieldNote: Her preferred payroll bridge remains **thinking work** exposed to AGI, and no advertised vacancy is guaranteed.
She distinguishes paid shifts still offered from a **post already ended**, when the reserve and lender call become necessary.

steps.text: Cancel sofa and deposit monthly instalment while wages continue
Keep offered paid tax shifts until actual end
After loss seek posted payroll job with written mortgage-covering wage hours start and pickup
After loss use reserve during search and ask lender for arrangement before missing mortgage bill

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Five years gives me a chance to test what clients will still pay an accountant to explain. Our tax calculations face AGI in 2031; capable robots arrive around 2034, later for Paolo's physical deliveries.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask Inez for a paid client explanation slot on the rota, not a speech about adapting. I would tell colleagues to log which questions clients bring back after an automated draft.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think our return fees will shrink, but a genuinely paid advisory place might still exist for a while. We cannot pay for speculative courses when our emergency money is so thin.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would take one supervised bakery-owner tax meeting each month only if Inez assigns paid hours and the firm bills it. I would study the professional body's free dispute notes while keeping current paid returns; if the firm offers a defined advisory post and pays both course fees and study hours, I would enrol in its client-advice course. In the first year after 2031, if return hours disappear, I would seek a posted advisory role only with written mortgage-covering wage, hours, start date and confirmed school pickup.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about losing paid checks, but I can test the client side before the deadline. Free notes and a real billable meeting are different from paying for a certificate on hope.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if Inez does not assign meetings?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep the paid tax files that remain and read the free notes at home. I would not invent billable demand from a friendly conversation in the queue.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Could Paolo cover more at home?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My partner Paolo can take pickup only when his depot confirms the delivery shifts. I would not accept new hours first and hope the children find their way home.

S3.quote: I would not invent billable demand from a friendly conversation in the queue.
fieldNote: She seeks **billable monthly cases** under supervision and refuses to count a queue conversation as a job path.

Read free notes; enrol in defined-role course only with funded fees and paid study hours
After lost hours take posted advisory job with written mortgage-covering wage hours start and confirmed pickup

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Ten years gives us time to shrink the mortgage before AGI reaches my tax desk in 2036. Robots around 2039 could change Paolo's deliveries later, but the accounts are thinking work and change first.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the firm to publish a paid training and staffing schedule, not an invitation to volunteer for extra clients. I would tell the children we plan around bills we can see, not a promised future job.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect the desk wage to be threatened eventually, yet ten years lets us lower what we owe. I would still be wary of a new title that takes me away from reliable paid returns too early.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the lender whether an extra fifty from each monthly wage could reduce principal without a penalty, only after regular bills and food are met; if there is a charge, I would deposit the fifty as cash instead. I would apply for a posted senior client role only if its written wage, hours and start date cover the mortgage and the confirmed pickup rota. In the first year after 2036, if tax work ends, I would take a qualifying offer and keep any remaining paid shifts until it starts.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about our thin savings now, though the long timetable gives us room to reduce debt. Ten years does not put this month's grocery money in the bank.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Could you stop working earlier?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No, my chartered qualification is valuable but it is not a pension. I need a paid role while the children and mortgage still depend on us.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Who confirms pickup?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My partner Paolo would check actual depot hours before we agree to a new rota. A job with a better title cannot leave our youngest waiting outside school.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most. Our main wage could fall before we have even a month's cash, so a notice period, real severance and posted work with written pay would help; a lender who speaks to us early would help too.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask whether Paolo's depot will still offer the same shifts once robots reach deliveries. I can plan for my desk loss in 2028, but I cannot promise my partner Paolo's hours in 2031.

headlineQuote: I can plan for my desk loss in 2028, but I cannot promise my partner Paolo's hours in 2031.
portrait: Nora is a **43-year-old senior accountant** with a master's and chartered qualification who leads tax work.
She is paid **below peers**, has under one month saved, and few nearby firms could replace her wage.
She uses **AI occasionally** for drafts but checks figures herself and wants signed evidence before wider use.
She tests **billable client work** and funds learning only when fees and paid time are covered.
Her **partner Paolo** works variable delivery shifts, while their two school-age children need a reliable pickup plan.
biggestWorry: The **2028 AGI** scenario could remove her main wage before the household builds savings.
whatWouldHelp: She wants **notice and severance**, posted paid work and early lender contact if the wage ends.
